STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of cut melon (cantaloupe) pieces on a square white plate, photographed from directly above.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square plate is about 24 cm across its diagonal-ish width, or roughly 21 cm per side. Its area is about 400 cm² (rounded corners reduce it slightly).

STEP 3 - Items: About 9 cantaloupe chunks. No sauce or oil is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The chunks sit in the middle of the plate and cover roughly 60 cm², or about 15% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: The chunks are about 1.8 cm thick. Gross volume is 60 × 1.8 ≈ 108 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut fruit has a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml, which gives about 65 g. As a check, each chunk is about 5 × 2 × 1.8 cm, or about 18 ml. Nine chunks make about 160 ml at solid density, but the plan view shows some are smaller, so about 100–110 g seems more likely. I'll use 100 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cantaloupe has about 34 kcal per 100 g, so 100 g gives about 34 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 100 g is plausible for a small serving of melon (roughly 9 chunks) on a large plate.
